items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And he and his brother and I were very good friends. We was on a long tour, you see, with Don Redman, you understand.

ctx.x: So he said -- he seemed to like tap dancing. He said you're a very good tap dancer, but you don't dance -- you don't tap dance like George Hillman. I said, well, no, darn, I said well I'm his teacher, you see. See. Said I used to be -- we were just room buddies, I says. And he and his brother and I were very good friends. We was on a long tour, you see, with Don Redman, you understand. The jazz giant little giant. Jazz giants.

And so, he says that he liked tap dancing. He said, 'What do you think I should do?' (unintelligible). He said, 'What kind of show would I use?' He says 'I wants to teach these people a lesson by trying to disturb deformation (unintelligible) being fraudulent, you see. In other words, they're trying to -- like "Dames at Sea" now, he had -- see, they tried to take his story idea, you know, and he wasn't having it. And his mother -- I mean she was kind of ill at the time, afflicted. But everybody -- Like I said, it…
